context: Interactive CPU flame chart profiler — a data visualization showing synthetic call stack profiles across 8 modules over a 10s window, with click-to-zoom and breadcrumb navigation
first_impression: Clean and functional with a thoughtful color palette, but the chart occupies only the top third of the viewport, leaving a large dead white zone that makes the overall page feel unfinished
what_works: Deliberate use of the Paul Tol qualitative palette (not schemeCategory10) gives the module colors genuine harmony and distinctiveness; the interaction design is sophisticated — LOD label rendering, smooth zoom transitions, hover outlines, and breadcrumb navigation all feel considered
what_doesnt: The chart renders into roughly 35% of the visible viewport with empty white below — a layout sizing issue that is the first thing a viewer notices; typographic hierarchy is minimal (16px bold title vs 12px gray subtitle is a modest step), and at default zoom the upper rows collapse into an unreadable mass of pixel-thin colored fragments with no visual entry point
